derivation_notes: For E + S <-> ES -> E + P, applying enzyme conservation and the initial-rate quasi-steady-state approximation gives [ES] = E_total*S/(K_M + S). Since v0 = k_cat*[ES], the rate is nonnegative, increases with S, and approaches the finite capacity k_cat*E_total.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

scenario_text: Measure the initial catalytic rate of a purified enzyme over a range of substrate concentrations while holding enzyme abundance and buffer conditions fixed. Reversible substrate capture creates a finite pool of occupied active sites, so the rate rises rapidly at low substrate and approaches a capacity limit at high substrate. Product accumulation is negligible during the measurement window, making each observation an independent instantaneous-rate experiment.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes substrate only forms the productive Michaelis complex. Relaxing that assumption to allow a second substrate molecule to bind nonproductively gives the standard substrate-inhibition initial-rate law, where high substrate increasingly diverts enzyme into a catalytically incompetent complex.
change_summary: Added one finite inhibitory binding scale K_I so the rate retains Michaelis-like behavior at low S but develops extra downward curvature at high S. This is a law refinement of the S-to-v0 response caused by substrate inhibition during the same initial-rate experiment.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All active sites are equivalent and act independently with a single productive substrate-binding mode and no substrate-dependent self-inhibition.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Substrate inhibition via additional nonproductive substrate binding at high substrate concentration, reducing the fraction of enzyme in the catalytically competent complex during initial-rate measurements.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As K_I -> oo, or whenever sampled S << K_I so that S**2/K_I is negligible, the expression reduces to the parent Michaelis-Menten law.

response_change.parent_relation: With S varied and k_cat, E_total, and K_M held fixed, v0 is a rectangular hyperbola with a single half-saturation scale K_M and fixed low-S slope k_cat*E_total/K_M.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that all active sites bind and turn over substrate independently with one shared affinity scale by allowing mild substrate inhibition from a second, nonproductive substrate interaction at higher S, so the S-to-v0 map bends away from the parent hyperbola after the initial rise.
response_change.observable_effect: Across a substrate sweep at fixed enzyme and buffer conditions, the child agrees with the parent at low-to-moderate S but shows reduced approach to saturation, or a broad peak followed by flattening/decline at higher S, which one Michaelis-Menten curve with one shared parameter set cannot reproduce.

evolution_contract.assumption_before: All active sites are equivalent and act independently with a single productive substrate-binding mode and no substrate-dependent self-inhibition.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: A second, nonproductive substrate-binding mode becomes occupied at high substrate and lowers the catalytically competent enzyme fraction during the initial-rate measurement.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As K_I -> oo, or for sampled S far below K_I, the inhibitory term vanishes and the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent: with only S varied and k_cat, E_total, and K_M fixed, v0(S) is strictly monotone increasing and approaches a plateau set by k_cat*E_total. Child: under the same substrate sweep and fixed enzyme/buffer conditions, v0 initially follows the same Michaelis-like rise but, once S reaches the inhibitory scale, develops stronger downward curvature, with reduced high-S rate and possibly a broad maximum before decline. This is a changed scored mapping from supplied input S to target v0, observable only when the experiment includes sufficiently high substrate relative to K_I.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters cannot absorb this change across the stated conditions because every positive-parameter Michaelis-Menten curve remains strictly increasing with one asymptotic plateau and no high-S downturn. A single parent parameter set therefore cannot simultaneously preserve the low-S slope and fit suppression or a peak at high substrate generated by nonproductive substrate binding.

evolution_plan.rationale: Varied condition: initial substrate concentration S is swept over a wide range. Held fixed: E_total and the buffer environment, with negligible product accumulation as in the parent setup. Parent response relationship: a monotone rectangular hyperbola with one fixed threshold scale K_M and no extra high-S curvature beyond saturation. Child response relationship: the same low-S rise is retained, but at sufficiently high S an extra substrate-dependent nonproductive occupancy reduces productive turnover, producing stronger downward curvature than the parent and potentially a broad maximum. This changes the scored target mapping v0(S), not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The contrast is scientifically admissible for enzymes known to exhibit substrate inhibition when substrate reaches concentrations comparable to an inhibitory binding constant; if experiments never access that regime, the refinement may be practically unidentifiable and the parent remains adequate there. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot simultaneously match the low-S slope and the high-S suppression/peak because Michaelis-Menten is strictly monotone increasing to a plateau for all positive parameters and lacks the extra curvature needed at high substrate.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.K_I: positive; vary across assay conditions from values comparable to the upper end of the substrate sweep to much larger when inhibition is weak

derivation_notes: The mechanistic rate law is unchanged, but the previous assumption that the inhibitory binding equilibrium is fixed across all assays is relaxed. Environmental changes such as pH, ionic strength, or cosolutes can alter the stability of the nonproductive enzyme-substrate complex, so K_I is promoted to a controlled condition while the rapid-equilibrium initial-rate framework is retained.
change_summary: The successor changes K_I from a fixed dataset parameter to an independently varied assay input, yielding a two-input target mapping v0(S, K_I). This creates condition-dependent shifts in peak position and high-substrate downturn strength that a single globally fixed K_I cannot reproduce across runs.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Temperature, pH, and ionic composition are fixed strongly enough that the nonproductive binding equilibrium encoded by K_I is constant across experiments.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Condition-dependent stabilization or destabilization of the inhibitory enzyme-substrate complex changes the effective substrate inhibition constant while preserving the same rapid-equilibrium initial-rate framework.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent for any experiment set in which K_I is held fixed across all assays; additionally, in the weak-inhibition limit K_I -> infinity over the sampled S range, the inhibition branch becomes negligible.

response_change.parent_relation: With buffer conditions fixed, v0 depends only on S through a single substrate-inhibition curve with one shared peak position and one shared high-S decline shape set by K_M and K_I.
response_change.child_relation: Release the inhibition constant from a fixed parameter to an experimental input so the v0-S curve changes with environment: the onset and strength of the high-S downturn vary across conditions while the low-S Michaelis rise can remain similar.
response_change.observable_effect: Across assays performed at different inhibition conditions, the substrate concentration giving maximal rate and the severity of high-substrate suppression shift systematically; one globally refit parent curve cannot match both weak-inhibition and strong-inhibition datasets simultaneously.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the experimental condition changes the effective substrate-inhibition strength so that K_I differs across runs and the substrate sweep reaches S comparable to or above K_I; if S << K_I for all conditions, the refinement is weakly identifiable.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest condition-dependent shifts in the high-S rolloff are visible; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to more separated K_I values, producing larger shifts in peak location and tail suppression without altering the basic low-S rise.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when K_I is held fixed across all experiments, or in the weak-inhibition limit K_I -> infinity over the sampled S range.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: The omitted effect is not a new dynamical state but variation in inhibition strength across independently prepared assay conditions. Keeping K_I fixed forces a single shared downturn shape, which cannot represent condition-dependent substrate inhibition with one parameter set.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Condition-dependent stabilization or destabilization of the inhibitory enzyme-substrate complex changes the effective substrate inhibition constant while preserving the same rapid-equilibrium initial-rate framework.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The structural increase comes from changing the scored map from a unary curve v0(S) to a two-input nonlinear surface v0(S, K_I), where S and K_I combine inside the inhibitory denominator term before the overall rational nonlinearity determines the rate. This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the environment now changes the location and severity of the high-S downturn rather than merely rescaling one shared curve.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: K_I is a fixed parameter shared by all assays.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: K_I is an independently varied assay condition reflecting environment-dependent inhibitory binding strength.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The child recovers the parent whenever K_I is held constant across the dataset, with the parent value identified as that fixed condition.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With S varied within each run and K_I varied across runs while k_cat, E_total, and K_M are held fixed, the child predicts a family of substrate-inhibition curves whose maxima move to higher S and whose high-S tails become less suppressed as K_I increases. The parent permits only one shared peak scale and one shared downturn shape because it maps S alone to v0 with a fixed K_I.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Allowing all existing parent parameters to refit once globally still leaves only a single fixed K_I, so the parent can generate only one common inhibition onset and one common high-S decline across all conditions. Matching separate weak- and strong-inhibition datasets would require refitting K_I separately by condition, which is exactly the promoted input and therefore not an admissible shortcut under a single parent parameter set.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the substrate-inhibition constant is invariant across all assays, even though nonproductive substrate binding is often buffer- and condition-sensitive.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Temperature, pH, and ionic composition are fixed strongly enough that the nonproductive binding equilibrium encoded by K_I is constant across experiments.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Condition-dependent stabilization or destabilization of the inhibitory enzyme-substrate complex changes the effective substrate inhibition constant while preserving the same rapid-equilibrium initial-rate framework.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with S varied and enzyme abundance fixed, rate rises approximately linearly at low S, saturates, then declines at high S with a single peak and a single inhibition scale controlled by one fixed K_I. Proposed child change: keep the same mechanistic form of inhibitory occupancy but allow K_I to vary as an independently sampled assay condition, so the target mapping becomes v0(S,K_I). Varied condition: substrate concentration S within each run and inhibition condition through K_I across runs; held fixed within a run are E_total, k_cat, K_M, and the initial-rate protocol. Observable contrast: at larger K_I the curve peaks later and declines weakly, whereas at smaller K_I the peak occurs at lower S and the high-S rate is more strongly suppressed. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both contrasts across those conditions because refitting K_I separately per condition is exactly the added freedom being claimed; one shared fixed K_I gives only one common peak scale and one common tail shape. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. Scientifically admissible activation requires assays spanning S values near the relevant K_I values; otherwise all curves collapse to near-Michaelis-Menten behavior and the refinement is not strongly testable.

derivation_notes: A new environmental input H modulates the catalytically competent fraction of enzyme through a sigmoidal protonation-like factor, while preserving the parent's rapid-equilibrium substrate inhibition structure. The correction vanishes at the reference condition H = 0, so the parent law is recovered exactly there.
change_summary: Added explicit buffer/environment control of catalytic competence as an H-dependent nonlinear modulation of the parent substrate-inhibition rate law. This introduces a measurable substrate-by-environment interaction across sweeps performed at different buffer conditions.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: A buffer/environment variable such as proton activity directly changes the fraction of enzyme in a catalytically competent state, altering effective turnover in addition to any condition dependence already represented through K_I.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: When H = 0, or more generally when the environmental modulation factor 1/(1 + (H/K_H)**n_H) is effectively 1 over the assayed range, the added term vanishes and the parent law is recovered exactly.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: Across substrate sweeps at different H, the low-to-intermediate-S slope and the inhibited peak height shift systematically with H, yielding an explicit S-by-environment dependence that the parent cannot express with one shared parameter set.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps v0 only from S with K_I treated as an externally supplied condition label, so at fixed parameter values the substrate-response shape has no explicit dependence on another assay variable that directly perturbs catalytic competence.
response_change.child_relation: Introduce an explicit environmental input that changes the productive catalytic fraction or turnover within the same initial-rate experiment, creating a non-separable dependence of v0 on S and the new condition because the environmental effect is amplified near the rising and peak regions set by substrate occupancy and inhibition.
response_change.observable_effect: Across assays where substrate is swept while buffer composition is held fixed within each sweep but varied between sweeps, the low-to-intermediate-S slope and the height/location of the inhibited peak shift systematically with the environmental input; one shared parent parameter set that ignores that input cannot reproduce those coordinated cross-condition shape changes.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when an independently varied buffer factor such as proton activity or ionic strength changes catalytic competence enough to alter turnover or productive-complex fraction over the same substrate range where S is comparable to K_M and/or K_I; weak effects or S far below both scales make the contrast hard to see.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, sweeps over S at a few environmental settings show different peak heights and rising-region slopes; in holdout, interpolation or modest extrapolation in that environmental variable reveals the same S-by-environment interaction rather than a mere constant rescaling.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the new environmental modulation is absent, negligible, or fixed to a reference condition so the added dependence collapses to a constant and the original substrate-inhibition law remains.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: Existing inputs contain S and condition-specific K_I only; they cannot represent an independently sampled environmental variable that alters catalytic competence without being absorbed ambiguously into a single refitted parameter per condition.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: buffer/environment control of catalytic competence through protonation-like gating
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A buffer/environment variable such as pH directly modulates the fraction of enzyme in the catalytically competent protonation state, changing effective turnover within the same rapid-equilibrium substrate-binding framework.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The child combines declared quantities H and K_H inside a nonlinear Hill-type map and applies that nested nonlinear factor as an added correction to the occupancy-dependent parent rate, producing an explicit interaction surface over S and H rather than a coefficient-only change.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Temperature, pH, and ionic composition are fixed.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: One buffer/environment variable is explicitly varied and modulates the catalytically competent fraction while the substrate inhibition mechanism remains in force.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set H = 0 so 1/(1 + (H/K_H)**n_H) = 1 and the added term is exactly zero, recovering the parent expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Across assays where substrate is swept while buffer composition is held fixed within each sweep but varied between sweeps, the low-to-intermediate-S slope and the height/location of the inhibited peak shift systematically with the environmental input; one shared parent parameter set that ignores that input cannot reproduce those coordinated cross-condition shape changes.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this because the parent expression has no H dependence at all, so it predicts the same v0 for all H values when S and K_I are fixed. Refitting existing coefficients once across all conditions cannot create the required cross-sweep response to H, and changing only K_I cannot generally capture direct catalytic-competence modulation when K_I is already supplied independently.

response_change.observable_effect: Across assays where substrate is swept while buffer composition is held fixed within each sweep but varied between sweeps, the low-to-intermediate-S slope and the height/location of the inhibited peak shift systematically with the environmental input; one shared parent parameter set that ignores that input cannot reproduce those coordinated cross-condition shape changes.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when an independently varied buffer factor such as proton activity or ionic strength changes catalytic competence enough to alter turnover or productive-complex fraction over the same substrate range where S is comparable to K_M and/or K_I; weak effects or S far below both scales make the contrast hard to see.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, sweeps over S at a few environmental settings show different peak heights and rising-region slopes; in holdout, interpolation or modest extrapolation in that environmental variable reveals the same S-by-environment interaction rather than a mere constant rescaling.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the new environmental modulation is absent, negligible, or fixed to a reference condition so the added dependence collapses to a constant and the original substrate-inhibition law remains.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: Existing inputs contain S and condition-specific K_I only; they cannot represent an independently sampled environmental variable that alters catalytic competence without being absorbed ambiguously into a single refitted parameter per condition.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model lets assay conditions affect only the inhibition constant K_I, omitting direct environmental control of catalytic turnover or productive-complex competence that is common across enzyme assays.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Temperature, pH, and ionic composition are fixed.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A buffer/environment variable such as pH directly modulates the fraction of enzyme in the catalytically competent protonation state, changing effective turnover within the same rapid-equilibrium substrate-binding framework.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already captures a single substrate-response curve with inhibition, and can shift that curve through K_I, but it assumes all other environmental effects are fixed. A realistic next refinement is to release one assay condition as an explicit input because enzyme catalytic competence often depends on pH or ionic composition, not only on inhibitory-complex stability. Vary the new environmental input between substrate sweeps while holding E_total and the within-sweep buffer condition fixed; compare v0 versus S across those sweeps. The parent with one shared parameter set cannot respond to that new input at all except by pretending all environmental effects are encoded solely through K_I, which cannot generally match coordinated changes in both the low-S slope and the peak/plateau behavior when the environment changes productive turnover in addition to inhibition. The effect is scientifically admissible when the environmental variation is moderate enough to preserve enzyme integrity and rapid initial-rate conditions, and strongest when S traverses the occupancy and inhibition scales. Limitation: if the chosen environmental range only weakly perturbs catalysis or acts exclusively through K_I, then this refinement may offer little observable gain.

derivation_notes: The initial-rate framework is preserved, but the assumption that substrate binding affinity is independent of the environmental condition is relaxed by replacing K_M with an H-dependent apparent binding scale K_M*(1 + H/K_H). This captures protonation- or conformation-dependent shifts in substrate association/dissociation energetics while retaining the same substrate-inhibition and catalytic-competence mechanisms.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The Michaelis constant K_M is independent of the environmental condition H, so H modulates only catalytic competence and not substrate binding affinity.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Environment-dependent protonation or conformational preorganization changes substrate binding energetics, making the apparent Michaelis scale vary with H during initial-rate measurements.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At the reference condition H = 0, the apparent binding term becomes K_M*(1 + H/K_H) = K_M, recovering the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The current law multiplies a substrate-inhibited Michaelis term by an H-only catalytic-competence factor, so H changes only the overall active fraction and does not alter the substrate scale or shape of inhibition except through the externally supplied K_I.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the assumption that pH/environment affects only catalytic competence: let the same environmental condition H also shift substrate binding affinity, so the apparent Michaelis scale changes with H and the v0-versus-S curve moves horizontally as well as vertically.
response_change.observable_effect: Across assays where H is swept at fixed E_total, k_cat, and supplied K_I, low-substrate sensitivity and half-saturation shift with H; two H conditions can have similar high-S plateaus after refitting gain but different initial slopes and midrange curvature, which the parent cannot reproduce with one shared parameter set unless K_M is allowed to vary with H.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when H is varied across values below and above K_H and substrate measurements include the low-to-mid range S ~ K_M, where horizontal shifts in apparent affinity are not masked by full saturation or dominant S^2/K_I inhibition.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, H-dependent vertical suppression is already visible; extending to holdout with broader H sweep and substrate values near K_M reveals that the low-S slope and midrange bend change with H in a way not captured by a pure multiplicative H gate.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that environmental modulation of binding affinity vanishes, so K_M becomes H-independent.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Environmental control of both catalytic competence and substrate binding affinity in a substrate-inhibited enzyme initial-rate assay
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Environment-dependent protonation or conformational preorganization can change substrate association/dissociation energetics as well as catalytic competence, making apparent affinity condition-dependent during initial-rate measurements.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because H is combined with K_M inside the nonlinear saturation denominator before the inhibition and competence nonlinearities act, so the environmental effect is no longer a separable output gain.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: H changes only catalytic competence while K_M remains fixed across environmental conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: H changes both catalytic competence and the apparent Michaelis binding scale through K_M*(1 + H/K_H).

evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H) + S + S**2/K_I) + k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H) + S + S**2/K_I)*(1/(1 + (H/K_H)**n_H) - 1)
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: At H = 0, K_M*(1 + H/K_H) reduces to K_M and the full expression becomes the parent exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response: at fixed supplied K_I, varying H only rescales the entire v0(S) curve by the same competence factor, so normalized curves versus S collapse and the half-saturation location set by K_M does not move. Child response: varying H changes both vertical activity and the substrate concentration range over which rate rises, producing an H-by-S interaction in the scored target mapping itself. Distinguishing condition: sweep H across below-to-above K_H while holding enzyme amount and buffer composition otherwise fixed and measuring rates for S spanning below and around K_M; then compare two H levels with similar high-S capacities after gain refitting but different low-S slopes or midrange curvature. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce such horizontal displacement because its H dependence is separable from S except through the already supplied K_I input. This is scientifically admissible when H perturbs ionization states involved in binding without denaturing the enzyme; if H only affects chemistry after binding, the refinement may be weak, and the parent is recovered.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters with one shared parameter set cannot absorb this change across the stated H sweep because the parent keeps H outside the Michaelis denominator except through the separately supplied K_I input, so H only applies a separable vertical modulation to one fixed S-shape. The child places H inside the saturation threshold, making low-S slope and midrange curvature change with H even when high-S rates are similar. That changed target mapping cannot be reproduced by a single parent parameter set unless K_M itself is allowed to vary with H, which is exactly the released assumption.

Hold E_total, k_cat, and other assay conditions fixed; vary H across below-to-above K_H and compare low-S assays with assays near saturation or substrate inhibition. In the parent, one refitted parameter set still predicts the same H midpoint structure across substrate regimes because all H-effects are tied to one K_H. In the child, the apparent H midpoint or curvature of v0 can differ between low and high S because denominator terms tied to binding/inhibitory occupancy respond to H differently from catalytic competence. This is scientifically admissible when H spans a range where protonation-linked changes are appreciable but enzyme integrity remains preserved. Limitation: if the sampled S range is narrowly confined to very low substrate, the contrast may be weak because affinity/inhibition contributions are then hard to observe.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Measure the initial catalytic rate of a purified enzyme over a range of substrate concentrations while holding enzyme abundance and buffer conditions fixed. Reversible substrate capture creates a finite pool of occupied active sites, so the rate rises rapidly at low substrate and approaches a capacity limit at high substrate. Product accumulation is negligible during the measurement window, making each observation an independent instantaneous-rate experiment.
promotion_reason: Existing symbols provide only one environmental scale K_H for all H effects. A distinct independently sampled condition is unnecessary, but one additional environmental-response input is needed if the benchmark requires separating the H sensitivity of binding/inhibition from that of catalytic competence without conflating them into the same shared transition.

response_change.parent_relation: The current mapping makes the environmental effect enter through one shared half-effect scale K_H, so at fixed substrate the H-dependence is a single Hill-like transition that uniformly rescales the Michaelis-Menten-with-substrate-inhibition rate.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the same environmental midpoint governs both catalytic competence and affinity/inhibition effects; allow the environment dependence already present in the denominator to have a distinct H-sensitivity from the numerator competence term, creating substrate-dependent bending of v0 versus H.
response_change.observable_effect: At low versus intermediate/high substrate, the H value where rate changes most strongly can shift, so normalized v0(H) curves no longer collapse to one common transition after simple rescaling.

diagnostic_groups.name: h_ratio
diagnostic_groups.role: Current environmental activation coordinate for the parent’s single shared transition scale

diagnostic_groups.name: occupancy_load
diagnostic_groups.role: Substrate-loading regime indicating whether apparent affinity terms can strongly shape the observed H-response

diagnostic_groups.name: inhibition_load
diagnostic_groups.role: Extent to which the nonproductive substrate-bound branch contributes to denominator curvature

activation_condition: Observable when H is swept across the transition region and substrate is varied from low occupancy (S comparable to or below K_M) into regimes where saturation or substrate inhibition matters (S comparable to K_M and/or sqrt(K_M*K_I) to above), so denominator and numerator H-effects are both consequential.
train_hidden_contrast: Within training, low-S assays mainly report catalytic-competence modulation, while higher-S assays expose the H-dependent affinity/inhibition curvature; in holdout, broader H sweeps or more strongly inhibitory S make the shifted H-response more pronounced.
continuation_path: Recover the parent by forcing the environmental midpoint/steepness governing affinity and inhibition changes to coincide with the catalytic-competence midpoint/steepness, or by making the extra distinction vanish so all H-dependence shares the same K_H transition.

dependent_variable.description: Initial product formation rate in micromoles per liter per second

independent_variables.description: Initial substrate concentration in micromoles per liter, approximated as the free substrate concentration

Condition-dependent effective substrate inhibition constant in micromoles per liter, treated here as an independently sampled assay input that captures environmental stabilization or destabilization of the nonproductive substrate-bound complex
Independently varied buffer/environment input representing proton activity or an equivalent catalytic-competence-modulating condition during each initial-rate assay
Independently sampled effective environmental half-effect value governing the H-sensitivity of apparent binding/occupancy terms in the denominator, in the same units as H

parameters.description: Catalytic turnover rate constant in inverse seconds
Fixed total concentration of catalytically active enzyme sites in micromoles per liter
Michaelis constant in micromoles per liter, equal to (k_off + k_cat)/k_on for the elementary binding and catalytic mechanism under the reference environmental condition
Half-effect value of the environmental input for catalytic competence modulation, in the same units as H
Dimensionless Hill-like steepness exponent for the environmental modulation of catalytic competence
